title: Absolute Ear — Ear training from intervals to composing
description: Ear training, reading music, rhythm and composing — all in one app. Build absolute and relative pitch like a game.
hero_title:
Ear training, reading music, rhythm & composing —
all in one app
hero_sub: Absolute and relative pitch training, played like a stage game. Grow your ear a little every day with Sori the fox.
aud1_d: Build up intervals, chords, melodies and chord progressions — the core of ear-training exams — stage by stage.
aud2_d: Lock in your pitch with sight-singing practice and loop the progressions you love.
aud3_d: Short stage games with Sori the fox make it easy to keep going a little every day.
feat_title: From listening to creating, in one app
feat1_d: Absolute pitch: name a note with no reference. Relative pitch: hear notes by their distance from each other. A short placement test finds the right starting point for you.
feat2_d: A Reading Music Basics course that starts with naming notes on the staff, plus rhythm training where you tap along to what you hear.
feat3_t: Sing, loop, and make your own
feat3_d: Sight-singing practice that checks your pitch through the mic, albums for repeat listening to intervals, scales and chord progressions, and the Music tab for writing your own.
game_title: Like a game, a little every day
game1_d: Open the map one stage at a time and see how far you have come at a glance.
game2_d: Your mascot cheers when you get it right and comforts you when you miss.
game3_d: Wrong answers cost a heart, so every question gets your full attention.
game4_d: Compete in the Weekly League with the XP you earn, and compare XP and trophies with friends.
faq1_a: Yes. Every training mode is free to start. When you run out of hearts, watch an ad or wait a bit for them to refill — or subscribe to Infinite Note for unlimited hearts and no ads.
faq2_q: Can I start with no music background?
faq2_a: Yes. A short placement test sets your starting point, and reading music starts from a basics course.
faq3_q: What is the difference between absolute and relative pitch training?
faq3_a: Absolute pitch training means naming a note you hear without any reference. Relative pitch training means recognizing notes by their relationship (interval) to a reference note. You can work on each separately in the app.
faq4_q: Will I lose my progress if I switch phones?
faq4_a: Link an account in the app and you can sign in on your new device to pick up where you left off.
faq5_q: How do I cancel my subscription?
faq5_a: Cancel any time from subscription management in the App Store or Google Play. You can also get there from the Shop screen in the app.
